original_value: Broadcasts of esport have come to function as technological intermediaries that shape how individuals engage with videogames in an everyday capacity. This article focuses on the moments of bodily tension when spectators of esport attempt to emulate techniques and strategies derived from broadcasts of esport matches. I present findings from a wider study which reveal three tensions: (1) antagonistic relations between players’ bodily faculties and techniques shown in esports, enculturated through esports’ popularity, and its perpetuation of bodily mastery and technological competency as key ways of engaging with videogames; (2) an inability to habituate the timings of body required in emulating high-level techniques and (3) the emergence of negative affective states – such as panic or anxiety – in attempting to replicate strategies. I propose the concept of ‘bodily finitude’ to describe and analyse these tensions.

result.paraphrase: Esports broadcasts have come to operate as technological mediators shaping how people engage with videogames in everyday life. This article examines the bodily moments of tension that arise when esports spectators try to imitate techniques and strategies drawn from esports match broadcasts. Drawing on findings from a broader study, I identify three tensions: (1) antagonism between players’ bodily capacities and the techniques displayed in esports, shaped by esports’ popularity and by its reinforcement of bodily mastery and technological competence as central modes of videogame engagement; (2) an inability to habituate the bodily timing needed to emulate high-level techniques; and (3) the appearance of negative affective states, such as panic or anxiety, in attempts to replicate strategies. I propose the concept of bodily finitude to describe and analyze these tensions.
